content:
Currently we have notation for

union : ∪    iUnion : ⋃    sUnion : ⋃₀
inter : ∩    iInter : ⋂    sInter : ⋂₀
  sup : ⊔      iSup : ⨆      sSup : -
  inf : ⊓      iInf : ⨅      sInf : -

(according to https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/naming.html#set)

I think it would be a good idea to add the last 2 entries for completeness. (Or at least document that they're missing?)

I just notice that for Set (Set α), then sInter coincide with sInf, and sUnion coincide with sSup.

Perhaps worth a note that, in this case, the sInter/sUnion spelling is preferred.

It may be relevant to mention that I have a PR that changes the underlying constant of the union/interoperations to be the same as for sup/inf (#42316). But that won't change the notation we use (and also won't change the naming of any constants). After that PR is merged, I'm planning to do the same for iUnion/iInter and sUnion/sInter. So then ⋃ and ⋃₀ will directly be notation for iSup and sSup, instead of this intermediate iUnion and sUnion.
In any case I think big square cup 0 should be a thing

Probably worth adding a note to Lean (the typeclasses for ⊆ are in Lean, not Mathlib) that some downstream project such as Mathlib is overriding the notation, such that ⊆ may either use one of the two typeclasses, depending on the type. On one hand, what Mathlib does is not Lean's problem, on the other hand Mathlib is popular enough that it may be worth the exception.

It's not quite right in this context to say ⋃₀ is “directly” notation for sSup (it is, but only for sets and similar types. Obviously one would only consider using ⨆₀ when not working with sets in the first place)
(not complaining, good to know about the subtlety of how some set notations are defined)
The repository containing the naming page is at https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/blob/lean4/templates/contribute/naming.md though.
